title: Savings by sequence length and user tenure matrix (workbook notes)
content:
Summary:
This workbook explores how KV/prefix cache economics vary when segmentation is performed jointly on request sequence length and user tenure. The goal is to identify high-leverage segments for targeted cache allocation (warm-start, prefetch depth, reserved slots) and estimate per-segment and portfolio-level cost reduction for hosted inference.

Top-level takeaways (provisional):
- Short sequences (<64 tokens) from long-tenure users show the highest KV hit rates per reserved slot — ~55–68% hit in our sample — and are the strongest candidates for low-latency prefix caching with small prefetch depth.
- Long sequences (>=512 tokens) generate most tokens but deliver lower prefix reuse; savings from aggressive KV allocation are smaller and require deeper prefetching to pay back.
- Mixed buckets (medium sequence, medium tenure) offer non-linear ROI: a modest increase in hitrate from 18% -> 28% can swing monthly savings from 4% to 12% of baseline.
- Recommendation: run a 4-week canary focused on the top 3 cohorts (Short/LongTenure, Medium/LongTenure, Short/NewUsers) with heatmap telemetry and enable automatic slot reallocation based on rolling 7-day hit-rate delta.

Methodology (brief):
- Source: sampled production request logs (Jan–Feb 2026), aggregated by user_id into tenure buckets, and by request into sequence-length buckets.
- Simulation: amortized per-token cost model (GPU seconds per token -> $/token baseline) + cache layer modeled with fixed slot budgets, TTL and prefetch depth knobs.
- Output: per-segment projected hit-rate, projected token reduction, cost with/without cache, and monthly savings.

Assumptions (editable cells in sheet):
- baseline_token_cost_per_1M = $1200  # (includes infra, amortized GPU + networking)
- avg_tokens_per_request_by_bucket = provided in data table below
- cache_slot_cost_monthly = $45  # amortized management overhead + memory per reserved slot
- prefetch_cost_multiplier = 1.15 for deeper prefetch (extra upstream CPU/IO cost)
- eviction_overhead_pct = 4%  # additional tokens re-computed due to eviction churn

Key formulas used in sheet (human-readable):
- projected_tokens_saved = total_tokens_in_bucket * kv_hit_rate
- savings_usd = (projected_tokens_saved / 1_000_000) * baseline_token_cost_per_1M - (cache_slots_allocated * cache_slot_cost_monthly) - prefetch_extra_costs
- ROI_monthly_pct = savings_usd / (baseline_cost_for_bucket)

Data preview (rows = sequence_length_bucket X tenure_bucket):
Columns: seq_bucket, tenure_bucket, requests_per_user_month, avg_tokens_req, users_in_bucket, total_tokens_monthly, median_prefix_hit, kv_hit_rate_sim, cache_slots_alloc, projected_tokens_saved, baseline_cost_usd, projected_cost_usd, savings_usd, savings_pct, notes
1, short (<64), long-tenure (>24mo), 520, 28, 42,000, 1.7M, 62%, 48%, 200, 34.0M, $40,800, $22,500, $18,300, 44.9%, "high reuse; small slots payback quickly"
2, short (<64), new-user (<3mo), 160, 22, 95,000, 2.1M, 35%, 28%, 120, 8.0M, $9,600, $6,700, $2,900, 30.2%, "burstier, lower per-user value but large population"
3, med (64-256), mid-tenure (3-24mo), 240, 140, 12,000, 1.68M, 22%, 18%, 80, 3.3M, $3,960, $3,400, $560, 14.1%, "sensitive to prefetch depth"
4, long (256-1024), long-tenure, 60, 820, 1,500, 1.23M, 10%, 8%, 400, 0.29M, $348, $310, $38, 10.9%, "low hitrate; deep seqs expensive to prefetch"
5, long (256-1024), new-user, 18, 980, 4,800, 4.70M, 6%, 5%, 120, 0.235M, $282, $270, $12, 4.3%, "not recommended for reserved slots"
6, med (64-256), long-tenure, 320, 180, 6,000, 1.08M, 28%, 22%, 240, 0.24M, $288, $150, $138, 47.9%, "good ROI if we prioritize long-tenure medium seqs"

Notes on numbers: these are illustrative samples; sheet includes full cohort matrix (5 seq buckets x 4 tenure buckets) and Monte Carlo toggles for hit-rate noise.

Sensitivity checks included in the workbook:
- Vary baseline_token_cost_per_1M ±20% -> sensitivity table shows portfolio savings change non-linearly; short-seq cohorts more sensitive to unit cost because they make up many small requests.
- Vary cache_slots_alloc pool from 100 -> 1000 (per-region) and recompute marginal ROI per slot. We observe diminishing returns around slot 500 for short/long-tenure cohort.
- Add eviction churn from 0% -> 10%: high churn kills ROI for medium/short cohorts especially when prefetch depth > 2.

Operational recommendations (actions & experiment plan):
1) Canary allocation: allocate 300 slots to Short/LongTenure and 150 to Med/LongTenure in us-west for 4 weeks. Track 7d rolling kv_hit_rate, latency p95, and upstream GPU consumption. Success criteria: >20% reduction in downstream token volume and positive ROI after slot cost for both cohorts.
2) Feature toggle for prefetch depth: A/B test control=depth1 vs variant=depth3 for Medium/LongTenure cohort. Measure delta in token savings vs prefetch_cost_multiplier. Abort if prefetch extra cost > savings margin after week 1.
3) Autoscaler policy: implement feedback that reassigns slots across cohorts weekly based on marginal ROI_per_slot ranking; cap per-cohort growth at +30% per week to limit oscillation.

Open questions & TODOs (workbook cells prefixed with TODO_):
- TODO_pop_model: Validate user churn model impact on long-tenure projected savings (Ravi).
- TODO_traceback: Instrument per-request prefix-length distribution to confirm assumptions about prefix re-use for short sequences (Liam).
- TODO_cost_basis: Confirm baseline_token_cost_per_1M with finance (Mae).
- TODO_ab_test: Wire up experiment flags and analytic events for prefetch depth AB test.

Links referenced in sheet:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPT/pages/8765
- Related sim code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-sim (PR #55 active)
- Opt ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPT-342

Appendix: example cell formulas to copy into workbook (Excel/Sheets):
- total_tokens_monthly = =users_in_bucket * requests_per_user_month * avg_tokens_req
- kv_hit_rate_sim = =IF(seq_bucket=\"short\", 0.45 + tenure_factor, 0.08 + tenure_factor*0.3)  # simplified pseudo-formula; actual sheet uses lookup table
- projected_cost_usd = =(total_tokens_monthly - projected_tokens_saved)/1e6 * baseline_token_cost_per_1M + cache_slots_alloc * cache_slot_cost_monthly * (1+eviction_overhead_pct)

Concluding note: this workbook is intentionally conservative on prefetch costs and eviction churn. If we can instrument real-time prefix re-use per-user and add a small warm-start cache at the edge, the measured hit-rates for long-tenure short-sequence cohorts may improve further and materially increase portfolio savings.

-- Aisha (workbook owner)
